Mr. Md. Mamtaz Uddin Ahmed, J:  Counter affidavit dated 26.8.2009 and Supplementary affidavit dated 12.11.2009 be kept with the record. 

2. The Rule was issued at the instance of the defendant Sree Sree Moha Parbhu and Sree Sree Gopal Jew Deities represented Sri Anil Chandra Nath Secretary, Executive Committee, calling upon the plaintiff opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment dated 7.8.1997 and 10.8.1997 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No. 173 of 1995 allowing the appeal and setting aside the judgment and decree dated 23.9.1995 and 30.9.1995 respectively passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Biswanath, Sylhet in Suit no. 49 of 1994 dismissing the suit for declaration of title should not be set aside and/ or pass such other order or further orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 
3. The Plaintiff Biresh Ranjan Dhar instituted Title Suit No.296 of 1969 in the Court of Munsef, 1st  Court, Sylhet which was re numbered as Title Suit No.49 of 1994 for declaration that the properties described in the schedule of the plaint are the personal properties of late Ramani Mohan Das Baishnab and the plaintiff is the only heir by inheritance of the said Ramani Mohan Das Baishnab and has been enjoying the said properties permanently and the plaintiff is entitled to the compensation money assessed by the government in respect of the 3"' schedule land described in the plaint and for permanent injunction. 

4. In the plaint, it has been started further that the schedule land had belonged to Ras Bihari Das alias Ramani Mohan Das who died intestate on 10th Cartik 1365 B.S. and he took possession of the property of schedule 1 and 2 after the death of said Rahmani Mohan and was growing paddy and was also enjoying the same. The said Rahmani Mohan Das during his life time created 2(two) debutter deeds dated 27th Chaitra 1333 B.S. 18' of Falgun 1351 B.S. respectively of the land described in the schedule of the plaint with intention to defraud his creditors. The said Ramoni Mohan had huge debts. The said deeds were created in the name of Sree Sree Mohan Prabhu and Sree Sree Sriman Gopal Jew Deties. In fact, the aforesaid deities had no existence at all and the aforesaid debuttar documents were never acted upon and that the suit properties were never treated as Debuttar properties during the life time of the donor Ramani Mohan Das. The creation of the alleged documents came to the knowledge of the plaintiff after his taking over possession of schedule 1 and 2 lands. The defendant no. 1 (since decased Brajangana Baishnabi) falsely asserted that the entire properties of Ramani Mohan Das was debuttar property and she was a Shebait. The suit land was recorded in the name of Ramani Mohan Das Baishnab as a secular property and he realized the Rent from the tenants by granting Largos (receipts) by filing rent suit in his own name. He also sold land to Asgar Ullah by registered deed dated 29 Maghs, 1358 B.S. in his personal capacity. The defendant No.1 Braja Bala Das meternal aunt of Ramanbi Mohan Das. She took her name as Brajangana Baishnabi and she was very cunning, while Ramani Mohan was simple and innocent person and used to live in the Akhra and taking advantage of Ramani's old age and simplicity and for deriving illegal gains managed to file 3 rent suits no. 42 43 and 44 of 1958 in the court of Munsif, 1st  Court, Sylhet in the name of the deities styling Ramani Mohan as Shebait, so that she being a Baishnabi might succeed him as next Shebait. The rents suit were filed to create evidence concerning the suit land that such land were debuttar Property. The said lady gave Ramani Mohan Das to understand that the property of the Baishnab will be taken by the Government and the only records for the same is to show the property as the debutter. After wholesale acquisition of rent receiving interest a sum of Ruppes 2001/86 paisa was assessed in the name of Ramani Mohan Das. The plaintiff after the death of Ramani Mohan filed objection and his name was recorded in place of Ramani in most of the IchatiAns including compensation assessment rolls. Said defendant No.1 Barja Bala Baishnabi filed title suit no. 301/1958 for permanent injunction for restraining the plaintiff from receiving compensation money from the government. In the said suit, the present plaintiff was restrained to get compensation until his title is declared in the properly instituted title suit. In the last week of May, 1969 the said Braja Bala in collusion with the avowed enemies of the plaintiff took step to dispossess him from the suit land, the plaintiff then constrained to file this suit. 

5. The defendant no. 1 contested the suit and added defendant nos. 15-19 also contested the suit by filing two separate written statements. There is no conflict of statements between two set of written statement. The defendant no. 1 and others denied all together the case of the plaintiff and stated that Ras Bihari Das alias Ramani Mohan Das Baishnab had considerable 
resource and he had money leading business as well as he was pious. He had been leading a life like a Baishnab and then he actually adopted Baishnab and took the name Ramani Mohan Das Baishnabi and he had installed the deities namely Gopal Jew Moha Prabhu Akhra of Raikhal in his own homestead and his homestead had turned into Akhra Bari which was known as Gopal Jew Moha Prabhu Akhra of Rakhail. To make a permanent arrangement for the maintenance of the Akhra and perpetual Sheba — puja Ramani Mohan Das made a gift of the major portion of his properties to the said deities on 27th Chaitra, 1333 B.S. He divested his interest in the debuttar properties and remained a founder Shebait of the deities. He acquired some properties by the income of previous debater and on 151 of Falgoon 1351 B.S. he made another deed of gift of some more properties and in the deed mentioned the time of successions of Shebait ship of deities and also mentioned some other terms for proper management. He never revoked or cancelled those deeds either expressly or by implication. During the last settlement and survey operation the suit properties with some other properties through mistake were 'recorded in his name Raman Mohan Das Baishnab (Ramani Mohan Das Baishnabi) without mentioning his name of the Shebait of the deities. Knowing this said Ramani Mohan filed application for correction of record of rights and rivisional case no.32 of 56-57 of the office of the A.D.C. (Revenue) Sylhet was started and an order was passed for such correction as prayed for but due negligence of some of the officials of the office of A.D.0 (Revenue) the order was not carried out and previous record continued without rectification and taking advantage of this wrong recording, the plaintiff with the influence of proforma defendant nos. 2-13 filed the suit for illegal gain and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

6. It has been stated further in the written statement of the defendant nos. 15-19 that after the death of the Ramani Mohan Das Baishnabi the defendant no.1 Baraja bala Baishnabi became the shebait as nominated by him as per custom before his death and she had been holding the office of Shebait of the deities and was maintaining possession of the property staying at the Akhra bari. During the War of liberation, Brajangana Bashnabi went to India and the movables and houses of the Akhra were looted by miscreants. After independence, Brajangana came to Akhrabari with broken health and expressed her desire to well wishers and matabbar of the locality that she will go back to India again to her relatives and will not come back. The Akhra was again looted by miscreants for which the properties of the deities were handed over to defendant No.19 to be kept at his homestead for safety and for regular Sheba-Puja. Hindu people of the locality had met on 23.5.1972 by a previous notice and they formed a working committee and in the said meeting defendant No.17 and 18 were nominated as president and secretary by the working committee and thereafter, they filed a Miscellaneous Case No.59 of 1972 under Section 5 of the Hindu Religious Endowment Act of 1863 in the Court of the District Judge, Sylhet and the learned District Judge allowed the Miscellaneous case against which the plaintiff filed Civil Revision Case No.1325 of 1973. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, High Court Division did not interfere but both the orders were affirmed by the High Court Division and further directed to dispose of the Title Suit within 6 months. The Defendant No.15 the Deities got exclusive right, title and interest in the suit land the plaintiff has got no possession in the suit land. The Defendants further stated that the Defendant No.14, government of Bangladesh submitted written statement in the suit on certain false and baseless averments which the answering defendants do not admit and prayed for dismissal of the suit with cost. 
7. The plaintiff examined 6 witnesses anti also produced documentary evidence in support of his case. On the other hand, the defendant examined 8 witnesses and also produced documentary evidence. 

8. The learned Assistant Judge heard the parties and examined the oral and documentary evidence produced by the plaintiff and the defendants and dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 23.9.1995 (decree signed on 30.9.1995). 

9. The plaintiff being dissatisfied with the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge preferred appeal in the court of District Judge, Sylhet being Title Appeal No.173 of 1995 and eventually, the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet heard the Appeal and allowed the same and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the Assistant Judge by his judgment and decree dated 7.8.1997 and (decree signed on 10.8.1997). 

10. Mr. Fazlul Haque the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant petitioners has taken us through the judgment of the courts below and evidence, both oral documentary as marked exhibits by the Trial Court and submitted that the learned Assistant Judge on proper discussions of the oral and documentary evidence decided the issue 'No.4 that the plaintiffs is not in possession of the suit property and that the deed- of gifts made in favour of the deities in the year 1333 and 1351 B.S. were acted upon, but the Appellate Court without properly adverted to the evidence has reserved those findings and that judgment being not a proper judgment of reversal has committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He further contended that issue No.6 and 7 were decided against the plaintiffs and that the Appellate Court has not reversed the findings of the Trial Court to the effect that the plaintiff had failed to produce any witness to prove the name of any creditor of late Ramani Mohan before the Court nor any name of any creditor was mentioned in the plaint to prove that the deed of gift in faour of the deities were executed and registered by Ramani to defraud the creditor and arrived at an erroneous findings which has resulted an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The Appellate Court has utterly failed to consider that Rash Behari Das became a Baishnab and not only be changed his name as Ramani Das Baishnab but also changed his life style and in doing so he and dedicated his property in the name of the deities and his homestead was turned into Akhra Bari which are being transpired from exhibit "Go Series" and that the Appellate Court also failed to notice that some of the properties were recorded in the name of the deities and some of the lands of Raekhail Mouja were recorded in the name of Ramani for which Ramani filed an application before the A.D.0 (Revenue), Sylhet for correction of record of rights in the name of the deities, which has been marked as exhibit-Cha and his intention thereby, was proved that he dedicated his whole life for religious purpose but the teamed Appellate Court arrived at an erroneous decision in setting aside the judgment of the Trial Court which has clearly caused failure of justice. The Appellate Court on the face of the record has erred in recording his self contradictory and misconceived findings while considering the evidence of PW.2 regarding Akhra Bah and also made findings as to Braja Bala Baishnabi without considering the evidence to its true perspective but arrived at an erroneous findings and decision and thus acted upon erroneous view which has occasioned failure of justice. He further contended that the Appellate Court has grossly misread the evidence of PW.2 and DW.1 in as much as the deities are now in the custody of the Shebait DW.1 in his own house and the homestead of Ramoni which is the Akhrabari has vacant house. Sheba-Puja of the deities has been performing by the committed approved by the learned District Judge but such fact and evidence were not correctly appreciated and came to the wrong finding which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He submitted further that the Appellate Court has come to wrong findings that Ramoni Mohan Das Baishnab during his life time realized rents from the tenants and also filed rent suits in his own name and from the exhibit 9(ka), 10-10(ka), it disclosed Ramoni himself did not implement the deed of gift in favour of deities are misconceived findings and those were not in issue before the court and recording finding beyond the scope of the suit has committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

11. The learned Advocate for the petitioner today has filed a supplementary affidavit and has taken ground No.10, 11, 12 and 13 in continuation of his grounds taken earlier in substantive Revisional Application and supporting the grounds very candidly submits that the Appellate Court has not at all reversed the finding of the Trial Court as to bringing of any witness to support basic contention of the plaintiff as to the creditors and also failed to appreciate the exhibit Ga(1) the application for correcting the S.A. Khatian contending that the schedule as stated in the application was not annexed with the application though the Trial court has recorded specific findings on those issues but the Appellate court has totally failed to reverse those findings and thus committed fundamental error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

12. The learned Advocate further contended that the trial Court has specifically recorded findings that the document of sale as stated in the plaint was not in the exhibit list and another document which has been produced before Trial Court and marked as exhibit-7 is not related to the debuttar property but such finding has not been reversed by the Appellate Court and Thus has committed error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate has also taken us through exhibit-"Uma", the order passed in Miscellaneous Case No.59 of 1972 by the learned District Judge and also placed exhibit-"Cha" the certified copy of the order passed in Civil Revision No.1325 of 1973 and submitted that those exhibits clearly show that the committee had held a meeting and the President and Secretary of the Committee were nominated to act and managed the affairs of deities by people of the localities and the learned District Judge upon considering the real position of the deities and also evidence had approved the committee and the said order had not been reversed by the High Court Division but the Appellate Court recorded no findings, what so ever, as to those exhibits and has committed error of law and prays for making the rule absolute. 

13. On the other hand Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, the Senior counsel along with Mr. Serajur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing before this court in countering the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner has strait way submitted that the basic question raised before this court as to whether 2 registered Debuttemama were acted upon during the life time of Ramoni Mohan Das Baishnabi and whether, the plaintiff is only serving heir of the said Ramoni Mohan Das and contended further that nature of the deeds also have to be cor_6idered before considering the oral evidence. He submits that the Appellate Court has clearly found that the deeds though executed by Ramoni Mohan were never been acted upon and held on consideration of the evidence both oral and documentary and the plaintiffs is the only surviving heir of late Ramoni Mohan, the Appellate Court since settled the facts being a final court of facts, these warrant no interference by the Hon'ble court and thereby, the Appellate Court committed no error of law in reversing findings of the Trial court. He further contends that on the face of the deeds, it is to be further decided and held, whether the two documents are "Illusory" endowments and also to be considered the evidence in that angle and in order to arrive at such conclusion the court has to consider the behavior of dedicator and the evidence in as much as Ramoni Mohan during his life time got recorded his name in S.A. Khatian (exhibit-2, 2(ka), 2(kha) and 2(Chaa) and sold land vide exhibit No.7 treating the properties as personal and secular properties and to ascertain such facts, the documentary evidence were not properly considered by the Trial Court but the Appellate Court has considered those aspect on the basis of the evidence both oral and documentary of the case and legally reversed the findings of the Trial court and committed no error of law. Referring to exhibit-14, it has been submitted that in a suit for realization of arrear rent filed Rent Suit No.44 of 1958 by Sree Mati Braja Bala Baishnabi and another, and the Munsif Court, Sylhet came to the findings :- "The plaintiff' have exhibited a debattaranama Ext.-I, the perusal of which shows that this property along with other properties, was gifted to deity but Exts. A-B a decree and copy of plaint in R.S. 182/52, show that donor Ramoni Mohan dealt with this property as his private property long, long after the execution of debatturnama. Thus it is clear that subsequent conduct of donor shows that debatturnama was not acted upon. So 1 am convinced that plaintiffs have no locustandi to bring this suit on the basis of debatturnama which was not acted upon." Against the said judgment the plaintiff Shebait Braja Bala took appeal before the District Judge, Sylhet being No.16 of 1959 (Ext.15). The appeal was heard by the Second Additional Court of Subordinate Judge, who affirmed the judgment of the Trial Court holding "The learned Trail Court accepted the defendant's contention as of substance and held that the Debuttarnarna Ext.-1 was not acted upon. 1 also find nothing to differ from him. Exhibits A and B conclusively proves the defendant's contention that Ramoni Mohan even after executing Debuttarnama in the year 1351 B.S. in respect of the jama and holding in brought Rent Suit No.182 of 1952 in respect of same jama and holding in his individual capacity giving an absolute go-bye to Ext.]. This shows clearly that this Ext.1 was not acted upon nor was it meant to be acted upon by Ramoni Mohan even during his life time "This contention- of the tenant, defdts was corroborated to the fullest extent by plff. No.2. But 1 may observe here that there is an apparent clash of interest between plff. No.1 and plff. No.2 and for that purpose I would like to leave the question of title of plff. No.1 and 2 interest open for a decision in a properly constituted suit between them as there is no scope for any finding of their title in the present suit or appeal." Referring to exhibit-7, the learned counsel submitted that the Trial Court committed error of law in finding contrary to the recital of the deed in as much as the Trial Court without considering the original deed has drawn conclusion on surmises but in fact Ramoni Mohan executed deed on 11.2.1952 and the schedule of both the deeds indicated that the preliminary number remains the same and in view of such facts the Appellate Court upon discharging the entire evidence held that the deeds were not acted upon and thus committed no error of law. He further contends that from exhibit-"Uma" it would be evident that the last alleged Shebait had come to Sylhet but did not convene meeting but the Hindu locals allegedly held the meeting on 23.5.1972 and in the meeting the alleged committee for the management of the property was formed and for the self same property the plaintiff filed suit before 1972 and the plaintiff was not notified while convened the meeting by the locals which is also evident from the exhibit "Uma" and alleged committee admittedly had formed in the absence of the plaintiff and this vital aspect of the case has not been considered by the Trial Court. The learned Counsel further submitted that from the evidence of the DWs it has been indicated that "idol" / deities had been shifted to house of the Secretary, the alleged Shebait and the Shebait is residing in his personal property and thus public has got no excess there. It would be evident further from the evidence that the alleged deitie's house of Akhara Bari has got no existence, what so ever, in spite of such evidence on record, such basic point, the Trial Court has not at all considered but this vital aspect of the case has been thoroughly considered by the Appellate Court and held that the deities have no existence and consequently, held that the deeds were not acted upon and therefore, committed no error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned counsel further submitted that the plaintiff is not bound by any action of the alleged committee to have taken after the filing of the suit in 1969 and such actions are bad in law and suffers from principle of Lis pendens, as completed under section 52 of the Transfer Property Act and the alleged recording of name of the alleged Shebait after 1969 has got no validity and as such, the plaintiff is not bound by such recording allegedly made in the name of the alleged deities, but such aspect of the case was not considered by the Trial Court. He submitted further that natural corollary is that admittedly the plaintiff is the only heir of Ramoni Mohan and after the death of Ramoni automatically, the title and the possession of the property had vested on the plaintiff, if no contrary title is established by producing any legal evidence and accordingly, the name of the plaintiff was recorded in the S.A. Khatian and paid the rents denying the existence of the deities, 
but this prime point of the case has also not considered by the Trial Court which has been considered by the Appellate Court and finally the learned Counsel prayed for discharging the Rule. 

14. To appreciate the legal position of the present case, it is felt incumbent to quote certain definitions such as :-
1. Creation of an endowment Any property, whether movable or immovable, can be validly dedicated for religious or charitable purposes, verbally or by writing. What is of paramount necessity is that the donor must divest himself of the property which he dedicates for religious or charitable purposes. Where a dedication is sought to be made by will, it has to be in writing and attested by two witnesses. The ceremony of SAMARPANA (i.e. delivery) is necessary for Creating a valid endowment. However SANKALPA (or formula of resolve) is not essential. 
2. Illusory endowment- Meaning of In the eye of law illusory endowment is no endowment, because its purpose is either deceptive or vague. It is void in consequence of uncertainly of purpose. It may also be void if it be violative of law or any public policy. A trust is not properly created in an illusory endowment. Where there is no real dedication of property but an attempt has been made to create a perpetuity in favour of donor's descendants, the gift to the deity is illusory. An illusory endowment is a sham endowment. In such endowment the donor does not divest himself of his rights in the property. Often the intention behind the creation of the endowment is to defraud the creditors or to evade other legal obligations. Whether an endowment is illusory or real can be ascertained from the true intention of the donor. 

3. Partial dedication — Meaning of.- In partial dedication, the donor does not divest himself completely of all beneficial interest in the property endowed. In such dedication, a charge is created on the property or a trust is created to receive and apply a portion of the income for the religious or charitable purpose. Mayne has Observed-"In such a case the property descends and is alienable and portable in the ordinary way, the only difference being that it passes with the charge upon it". Thus, partial dedication makes a devise of property for religious purposes but in truth the devise retains the beneficial interest.
4. Complete dedication- Meaning of.-In a complete dedication the bequest is made absolutely to an idol or to a religious or charitable institution and the donor completely divests himself of all beneficial interest in the property given in endowment." (The above definitions are quoted from "Mitra on Hindu Law" by Sunil Kumar Mitra, chapter 12, part-2 "Religious and Charitable Endowments" page-504) 

15. On examination of the judgment of the Trial Court, it appears that the Trial Court dismissed the suit holding:- 

"By a comparative study it is found that oral witness on behalf of the defendant are stranger than that of the plaintiff. Because they are very close to the suit land. And they have no direct interest in the suit land like that of the plaintiff's witness. Plaintiff's witnesses are plaintiff's purchaser. So it is held that the plaintiff could not prove his possession over the suit land. And it is further held that the gift deeds dated 1333 and 1351 B.S. are acted upon." and in settling the issue No.6 held:- 
"Plaintiff's maternal grand father dedicated the suit lands by two gift deeds and they had been acted upon, is settled in the aforesaid issues. So it is held that the plaintiff is not entitled to get decree of declaration and permanent injunction." 

16. On perusal of the judgment of the Appellate Court, it transpires that the Appellate Court has reversed the findings and decision of the Trial Court and held that the dedication to have made by 2 documents by Ramoni Mohan had not been acted upon as the donor had not completely divested himself of all beneficial interest in the property given in endowment and that the plaintiff is the legal heir of the said Ramoni Mohan and he has interest in the land and further held perusing the exhibits, in as much as the judgments of the litigations have expressly disclosed that Ramoni Mohan Das during his life time realized rent from the tenants and also for arrear of rents had filed rent suits and his name also was recorded in S.A. Khatian which is evident from exhibit-Gha(1) and further that such recording of rights has not been challenged 
holding that the application alleged to have submitted by Ramoni Mohan Das had not contained schedule in the application and no cogent evidence has been adduced to dislodge the exhibit-Gha(1) and also held that by the 2 documents Ramoni Mohan himself had not divested himself from his land and such endowments are not endowment according to in Hindu law and coming to such findings reversed the findings of the Trial Court and decreed the suit. 

17. In view of the aforesaid judgments, the prime question before us, whether the deeds admittedly executed by the Rash Behari Das alias Ramoni Mohan Das were acted upon. In view of judgment of reversal, I have very meticulously gone through the judgment of both the courts and also the oral and documentary evidence to arrive at my own findings. It appears, the Trial Court has interpreted the evidence in the light of the order passed in Miscellaneous Case No.59 of 1972, exhibits Cha, Chaa and Chaa(1) the resolution book. The order passed in Misc. Case No.59 of 1972 has clearly expressed that: 

"There is no scope for adjudication in this case whether Debuttar namas exhibits 2 and 2(a) were acted upon or not. This point will be canvassed and dedicated upon Title Suit No.296 of 1969 which is pending between the parties. So, 1 refrain from deciding whether the debuttarnama Exts.2 and 2(a) were acted upon or not." and approved the formation of working committee in the meeting held on 23.5.1973 corresponding to 9th Juista 1379 B.S. and that order was also approved in Civil Revision No.1325 of 1973 dated 2.2.1982. 

The Trial court upon considering the oral evidence held that the plaintiff produced the witnesses who are purchasers and interested witnesses and the plaintiff also did not produce any witness to support his contention that the dedication was made by said 2 deeds to avoid the creditors. 

18. The Appellate Court has held relying upon mainly on the S.A. Khatian exhibit 2-2('), sale deed dated 22/02/1952 exhibit 7 and order dated 5.1.1959 in rent suit no.44 of 1958 and also on the basis of the order passed in Rent appeal No.16 of 1959 (arose out of rent suit no.44 of 1958) that the plaintiff has been able to prove that during the life time of said Ramoni Mohan, he did not divest himself from the properties rather he mutated his name and realized rent. The A"ppellate Court also held that the plaintiff is admittedly the grand son of Ramoni Mohan and the title and possession naturally had vested in him. He also found that the deities were not kept in the Debuttar properties but allegedly preserved in the custody of the Secretary of the committee in his personal house and also found that alleged application made by Ramoni Mohan contained no schedule of the property and as such, recording of names in S.A. Khatian remained unchallenged and I am of the view that the Appellate Court has decided the matter to its true perspective considering the evidence both oral and documentary and law and in reversing the findings, it appears further that the Appellate Court has committed no error of law. I have also concentrated myself as to whether the deeds ' were acted upon and upon scrutiny found that the original maker of the deeds i.e. Ramoni Mohan had recorded his name in S.A. Khatian during his life time and Braja Bala tried to establish herself as the Shebait by filing rent suit but the Munsif, 1st Court, Sylhet in rent suit no.44 of 1958 which had clearly held that the deeds were not acted upon and such findings were affirmed by the Appellate Court with the opinion that in an appropriate constituted suit the fate of the deeds will be decided and accordingly, the plaintiff had filed the suit in 1969. It appears from the resolution of the meeting held on 23.5.1972 Braja Bala was not present. The life of the committee appears to have given by the learned District Judge till appointment of the Shebait and since the plaintiff has been able to prove that the dedication of properties made by Ramoni Mohan by 2 deeds were not acted upon and further held that the function of the committee thereby ceased and in holding as such, the Appellate Court has committed no error of law. It is in evidence that the del'ies are not being maintained in the land of the Debuttar property but kept in a private house of the Secretary and as such, the very purpose of dedication as it appears to have lost and as such, I am of the opinion that the plaintiff has been able to prove that the Endowments had been made were "Illusory endowments and "Illusory endowments" are sham endowments. In such endowment the donor does not completely divest himself of all beneficial interest in the property given in endowment. 

19. It has been found from the evidence on record that the Secretary of the Committee had removed the temple in which those were installed and installed those in his private house, where the member of the Hindu community appears to have no excess and thus, the worshippers are depriving in giving Sheba-puja. 

20. It has been abundantly clear that Brajangana had been acted as shebait for certain period and being in such position, she could appoint her successor but she did not appoint her successor and in that view of the matter, when she left the premises without exercising her power, the office of the shebait had automatically reverted to the plaintiff who is the only heir of the founder and such aspect of the case had not been noticed by the trial Court. The view of this court finds support in the case of Radha ' Nath Mukherjee Vs. Saktipada Mukherjee, (1936) 58. All. 

21. In view of my above discussion, I find no substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners but I find substance in the submissions of Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Counsel of the plaintiff opposite party. Consequently, I find the Rule has got no merit as the Appellate Court committed no error of law in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court which has occasioned no failure of justice. 

22. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree dated 07.08.1997 and 10.8.1997 respectively passed by the learned Additional District judge, 3' court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No.173 of 1995 allowing the appeal and setting aside the judgment and decree dated 23.9.1995 and .30.9.1995 respectively passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Biswanath, Sylhet in title Suit No.49 of 1994 dismissing the suit for declaration of title are affirmed. Consequently, the suit is decreed. 

23. Staying the order of operation of the judgment and decree given at time of issuance of rule is vacated. 

24. The office is directed to send down the lower courts records immediately.

End.
